newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Vendex reviews KBB stake sale.
newsitem.headline: Vendex reviews KBB stake sale.

text.p: Retailer Vendex International NV said on Friday it was reviewing the previously-announced sale of its stake in Koninklijke Bijenkorf Beheer (KBB), but was not yet calling off the deal, despite a sharp fall in KBB stock.

KBB shares fell almost 10 percent, or 13.50 guilders, to 128.50 guilders on Thursday, after it announced a profit warning just days after Vendex had said it would sell a 36 percent stake in the Dutch department store chain.
In early Friday trading KBB shed another 0.50 guilders to 128 guilders. Vendex dipped another guilder to 69.00 after losing 2.50 guilders on Thursday.
The KBB sell-off was due to be realised within two weeks in an international placement carried out by a syndicate led by Morgan Stanley.
"All parties involved will meet and consider the current situation," a Vendex spokesman said, adding that no decision was expected before the weekend.
He said it would have been better if KBB had told Vendex earlier that it was expecting lower 1996/97 net profit.
"It would be going too far to say we're quarrelling with KBB," the Vendex spokesman said in response to a report in Dutch daily Volkskrant that KBB and Vendex were in dispute.
Vendex has said it needs the cash from the KBB stake sell-off to expand its core business.
Analysts had valued the 36 percent stake at 595 million guilders before the KBB shares fell.
